headings.title: Offense of robbery in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines robbery in the first degree when forcibly stealing and causing serious physical injury, being armed with a deadly weapon, using or threatening a dangerous instrument, displaying what appears to be a deadly weapon, or stealing controlled substances from a pharmacy.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates robbery in the first degree as a class A felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 569.020 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of robbery in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines robbery in the second degree when a person forcibly steals property and causes physical injury to another person.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates robbery in the second degree as a class B felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 569.030 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of vehicle hijacking
headings.reviewNote: Defines vehicle hijacking when knowingly using or threatening physical force to seize or attempt to seize possession or control of a vehicle.

headings.title: Class B felony default classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates vehicle hijacking as a class B felony unless meeting criteria under subsection 3.

headings.title: Class A felony aggravating factors
headings.reviewNote: Elevates vehicle hijacking to a class A felony for serious physical injury, deadly weapons, dangerous instruments, or presence of a child or special victim.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (L. 2020 S.B. 600).

headings.title: Elements of stealing
headings.reviewNote: Defines stealing by appropriating property or services without consent or by deceit/coercion, attempting to take anhydrous ammonia or liquid nitrogen, or receiving stolen property.

headings.title: Class A felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies stealing as a class A felony if appropriated property consists of specified large containers or applicators containing anhydrous ammonia.

headings.title: Class B felony classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies stealing as a class B felony for anhydrous ammonia or liquid nitrogen, repeat livestock or captive wildlife over $3,000 (with 80% minimum prison term), repeat vehicle/watercraft/aircraft theft, livestock over $10,000, financial institution property taken physically from an individual, or organized retail theft of $10,000 or more.

headings.title: Class C felony classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies stealing as a class C felony for property/services of $25,000 or more, teller machines or contents, or organized retail theft between $750 and $10,000.

headings.title: Class D felony classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies stealing as a class D felony for property of $750 or more, taking from victim's person, motor vehicles, firearms, credit devices, records, controlled substances, or metal wire.

headings.title: Class E felony classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies stealing as a class E felony for animals, catalytic converters, three prior stealing offenses within ten years, or common carrier delivered packages.

headings.title: Class D misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates first-offense stealing of property valued under one hundred fifty dollars not otherwise specified as a class D misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor default classification
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that any offense of stealing not otherwise classified in the section is a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Pleading and proof of prior findings of guilt
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior findings of guilt for sentence enhancements to be pleaded and proven pursuant to section 558.021.

headings.title: Separate felony charging authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes treating appropriations of specified property categories or values of $750 or more as separate felonies charged in separate counts.

headings.title: Single criminal episode and aggregation of value
headings.reviewNote: Permits aggregating property or service values appropriated pursuant to one scheme or course of conduct into a single criminal episode.

headings.title: Definition of organized retail theft
headings.reviewNote: Defines organized retail theft covering agreements to steal, receiving stolen business property, and leading or financing commercial theft schemes.

headings.title: Prosecution authority of attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general upon written request by local prosecutor to prosecute organized retail theft at state expense.

headings.title: Limitation on attorney general powers
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no additional powers beyond commencement and prosecution of specified offenses are granted to the attorney general.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 14 subsections against archived text (2025 H.B. 495); clarified subsection 3 note for 80% repeat livestock minimum and financial-institution taking.

headings.title: Offense of feigned blindness
headings.reviewNote: Defines feigned blindness by simulating blindness to obtain something of value by deceit.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates feigned blindness as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 578.075 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of stealing leased or rented property
headings.reviewNote: Defines stealing leased or rented property by failing to return, concealing, unauthorized transfer, or nonpayment of agreed charges.

headings.title: Applicability to lease-purchase and rent-to-own contracts
headings.reviewNote: Applies section to all lease and rental agreements including lease-purchase and rent-to-own contracts, with ownership remaining in lessor.

headings.title: Evidence of intent and law enforcement reporting
headings.reviewNote: Establishes evidence of intent from false information or failure to return after written demand, with specific 72-hour reporting procedures for motor vehicles.

headings.title: Inoperable defective vehicle exception
headings.reviewNote: Exempts lessees of defective inoperable vehicles who notify lessor of vehicle location and defect within specified time.

headings.title: Concurrent offense of property damage
headings.reviewNote: Provides that destroying leased property to avoid return constitutes property damage in addition to a violation of this section.

headings.title: Venue for prosecution
headings.reviewNote: Establishes venue in the county where the personal property was originally rented or leased.

headings.title: Penalty classifications
headings.reviewNote: Designates stealing leased property as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class D felony if property value is seven hundred fifty dollars or more.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text; formerly section 578.150 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Appropriation of lost property
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that appropriating lost property is not stealing unless found under circumstances giving knowledge or means of inquiry as to the owner.

headings.title: Burden of injecting issue
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of injecting the issue of lost property upon the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-79).

headings.title: Claim of right defense
headings.reviewNote: Exempts appropriations made under honest belief of right or honest belief that owner would have consented.

headings.title: Burden of injecting issue
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of injecting the issue of claim of right upon the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of alteration or removal of item numbers
headings.reviewNote: Defines alteration or removal of item numbers with purpose of depriving owner of lawful interest.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates alteration or removal of item numbers as a class E felony if value is seven hundred fifty dollars or more, otherwise a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of forgery
headings.reviewNote: Defines forgery when making, altering, erasing, or using writings or other objects with purpose to defraud.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates forgery as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text and 2013 case annotation (State v. Diaz-Rey).

headings.title: Offense of filing false documents
headings.reviewNote: Defines filing false documents with intent to defraud, deceive, harass, alarm, or negatively impact financially.

headings.title: Penalty classifications and public official enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies filing false documents as a class D felony, elevated to class C felony for repeat offenses or when targeting public officials, judges, or officers.

headings.title: Materiality requirement for victim occupation enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Requires victim occupation to be material to the filing for penalty enhancements to apply, extending protections to retired personnel and family members.

headings.title: Mandatory restitution
headings.reviewNote: Mandates full restitution to victims for actual losses, payable in addition to any incarceration.

headings.title: Concurrent prosecution and retention exemption
headings.reviewNote: Preserves prosecution under other state or federal criminal laws and clarifies receiving entity retention duties.

headings.title: Fraudulent filing ledger and law enforcement notification
headings.reviewNote: Directs recording agencies to log suspicious filings, make ledgers available to prosecutors and law enforcement, and provide prompt notice.

headings.title: Judicial review petition for invalid filings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes filing a probable cause statement in court to seek judicial invalidation of fraudulent filings.

headings.title: Hearing schedule and recordation of invalidity ruling
headings.reviewNote: Requires initial hearing within twenty business days and fee waiver for recording invalidity rulings, and permits forwarding the ruling to credit bureaus or other institutions upon petitioner's motion at no additional cost.

headings.title: Assessment of court costs and fees
headings.reviewNote: Assesses court costs and fees against the original filer if the document is deemed invalid, with no extra fees if valid.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 9 subsections against archived text (L. 2018 H.B. 1769); corrected subsection 8 note to preserve permissive 'may be forwarded' for credit-bureau notice.

headings.title: Offense of possession of forging instrumentality
headings.reviewNote: Defines possession of a forging instrumentality when making or possessing tools to commit forgery.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates possession of a forging instrumentality as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Definitions for counterfeiting
headings.reviewNote: Defines counterfeit mark, intellectual property, and retail value.

headings.title: Offense of counterfeiting and presumption
headings.reviewNote: Defines counterfeiting goods or services and creates a presumption of possession for sale or distribution when possessing more than twenty-five items bearing a counterfeit mark.

headings.title: Misdemeanor default classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates counterfeiting as a class A misdemeanor except as provided in felony enhancements.

headings.title: Class E felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies counterfeiting as a class E felony for prior convictions or intermediate item quantities and retail values.

headings.title: Class D felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies counterfeiting as a class D felony for multiple priors, manufacturing, or exceeding quantity or retail value thresholds.

headings.title: Aggregation of quantity or retail value
headings.reviewNote: Requires aggregating the total quantity or retail value of items or services across all counterfeit marks.

headings.title: Remedies cumulative
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that criminal remedies under this section are cumulative to civil remedies.

headings.title: Registration certificate as prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Makes state or federal intellectual property registration certificates prima facie evidence of facts stated therein.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 8 subsections against archived text; tightened subsection 2 note to statutory 'presumed' wording.

headings.title: Seizure and forfeiture of counterfeit property
headings.reviewNote: Directs law enforcement seizure of counterfeit items and equipment used in violations, subject to forfeiture under chapter 513.

headings.title: Release or destruction of seized items
headings.reviewNote: Mandates release of seized counterfeit items to the intellectual property owner upon request, or destruction unless the owner consents to another disposition.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; included owner-consent alternative disposition in subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Offense of issuing false instrument or certificate
headings.reviewNote: Defines issuing a false instrument or official certificate by an authorized person knowing it contains false statements or is blank.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates issuing a false instrument or certificate as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text and 1996 case annotation (State v. Moriarty).

headings.title: Offense of passing bad checks
headings.reviewNote: Defines passing bad checks with purpose to defraud or failing to pay within ten days of written notice of dishonor.

headings.title: Definition and delivery of actual notice in writing
headings.reviewNote: Defines actual notice in writing, including summons, warrant, or refused communications.

headings.title: Aggregation of check amounts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggregating face amounts of bad checks passed within a ten-day period to determine the offense grade.

headings.title: Penalty classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies passing bad checks as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony for amounts of seven hundred fifty dollars or more or no account.

headings.title: Administrative handling costs and prosecution fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes administrative handling costs collected by prosecutors and fees for the Missouri office of prosecution services fund.

headings.title: Service charges by prosecutors and check holders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes prosecutors and private check holders to assess reasonable service charges and bank return fees.

headings.title: Condition of returned dishonored checks
headings.reviewNote: Requires financial institutions to return dishonored checks in substantially the same condition to identify the maker.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text; preserved mandatory fee collection in subsection 5 and permissive service charges in subsection 6.

headings.title: Offense of fraudulently stopping payment
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraudulently stopping payment on a check, draft, or debit device with purpose to defraud.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates fraudulently stopping payment as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony if face amount or same-course aggregate amount is seven hundred fifty dollars or more.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of violation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes prima facie evidence upon failure to make good payment or return property within ten days of written notice.

headings.title: Definition and content of notice in writing
headings.reviewNote: Specifies certified or registered mailing requirements and warning statements for notice in writing.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text; noted same-course aggregate $750 threshold in subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Offense of fraudulent use of credit or debit device
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraudulent use of a credit or debit device knowing it is stolen, revoked, unauthorized, or to avoid property taxes.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates fraudulent use as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony if value is seven hundred fifty dollars or more within thirty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of fraudulent procurement of credit or debit device
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraudulent procurement by false statements, unauthorized use of identity, or possession of a fraudulently obtained device.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates fraudulent procurement of a credit or debit device as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Business entity liability limitation
headings.reviewNote: Shields business entities from criminal liability for accepting applications or transactions absent clear and convincing evidence of conspiracy.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of gift card fraud
headings.reviewNote: Defines gift card fraud through tampering with cards, deceptive schemes to obtain redemption information, or unauthorized use.

headings.title: Class C felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies gift card fraud as a class C felony if the value obtained is twenty-five thousand dollars or more.

headings.title: Class D felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies gift card fraud as a class D felony if value is seven hundred fifty dollars or more but less than twenty-five thousand dollars.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification and valuation definition
headings.reviewNote: Designates gift card fraud under seven hundred fifty dollars as a class A misdemeanor and defines value as greatest economic loss.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (L. 2026 S.B. 1421).

headings.title: Offense of deceptive business practice
headings.reviewNote: Defines deceptive business practices committed recklessly in business, including false weights, short delivery, adulteration, and misleading ads.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates deceptive business practice as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of financial exploitation of elderly or disabled person
headings.reviewNote: Defines financial exploitation of an elderly person or person with a disability through deceit, coercion, undue influence, or false promises.

headings.title: Graduated penalty classifications based on property value
headings.reviewNote: Classifies financial exploitation from class A misdemeanor up to class A felony based on property value tiers.

headings.title: Preservation of domestic violence remedies
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that provisions do not limit statutory remedies available under domestic violence laws.

headings.title: Good faith defense for assistance
headings.reviewNote: Shields persons making good faith efforts to assist in property management from criminal liability.

headings.title: Bona fide estate planning exemption
headings.reviewNote: Protects bona fide estate planning and tax transfers that do not adversely impact the elderly or disabled person's accustomed standard of living.

headings.title: Mistake of age or disability not a defense
headings.reviewNote: Bars defense that the defendant reasonably believed the victim was not elderly or disabled.

headings.title: Unlawful withholding of facility resident funds and restitution
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits withholding funds of a Medicaid-eligible resident owed to a chapter 198 licensed facility, authorizes DSS record release, and permits prosecutors to request circuit court restitution (with 10% to prosecutor).

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text; replaced 'vulnerable persons' with statutory 'elderly or disabled person' in subsection 1 heading and clarified circuit court restitution role in subsection 7 note.

headings.title: Definitions for financial institution accounts fraud
headings.reviewNote: Defines financial institution and financial institution account.

headings.title: Offense of financial institution accounts fraud
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraud to cause withdrawals, transfers, or payments from financial institutions or customer accounts.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates financial institution accounts fraud under five hundred dollars as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Felony classifications based on culpable mental state
headings.reviewNote: Classifies fraud of five hundred dollars or more from class E to class B felony according to criminal negligence, recklessness, knowledge, or purpose.

headings.title: Alternative charging restriction
headings.reviewNote: Allows alternative charging but bars dual convictions for the same theft of moneys.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text (L. 2025 S.B. 98).

headings.title: Offense of commercial bribery
headings.reviewNote: Defines commercial bribery involving breach of fiduciary or professional fidelity, appraisal bias, or offering corresponding bribes.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates commercial bribery as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of defrauding secured creditors
headings.reviewNote: Defines defrauding secured creditors by destroying, concealing, or transferring secured property with purpose to defraud.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates defrauding secured creditors as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony if secured debt is seven hundred fifty dollars or more.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of library theft
headings.reviewNote: Defines stealing of library materials by unauthorized removal, improper card use, failure to return, or defacement.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence and replacement payment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes prima facie evidence upon failure to return within ten days of certified written notice without good cause, and treats replacement cost payment for an item of no historical significance as return.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; added 'item of no historical significance' qualification to subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Offense of misapplication of financial institution funds
headings.reviewNote: Defines misapplication of funds by financial institution officers, directors, agents, or employees.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates misapplication of financial institution funds as a class E felony, elevated to class D felony if amount is seven hundred fifty dollars or more.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of making false entries in financial institution records
headings.reviewNote: Defines making false entries in books, reports, or statements of a financial institution with intent to defraud or deceive.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates making false entries in financial institution records as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of check kiting
headings.reviewNote: Defines check kiting by drawing against uncollected funds and covering with another check drawn on insufficient funds.

headings.title: Definition of collected funds
headings.reviewNote: Defines collected funds as verified final payment or ten business days elapsed without return.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates check kiting as a class E felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of identity theft
headings.reviewNote: Defines identity theft by obtaining, possessing, transferring, or using identification not lawfully issued with intent to defraud.

headings.title: Penalty classifications based on value
headings.reviewNote: Classifies identity theft from class B misdemeanor up to class B felony based on the value of credit, money, or property obtained.

headings.title: Restitution for victim clearing costs and proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court-ordered restitution for costs and attorney fees to clear credit records or satisfy obligations.

headings.title: Civil action for statutory and actual damages
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil actions for injunctive relief, statutory damages up to five thousand dollars or treble actual damages, and attorney fees.

headings.title: Deceased person estate recovery
headings.reviewNote: Extends civil damage recovery rights to the estate of a deceased victim whose identity was misused.

headings.title: Statute of limitations for civil action
headings.reviewNote: Requires civil actions to be brought within five years from when the wrongdoer's identity was discovered or reasonably should have been discovered.

headings.title: Independence of civil remedies
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that civil actions do not depend on criminal prosecution and remedies are cumulative.

headings.title: Exempted activities
headings.reviewNote: Exempts minor age misrepresentation for alcohol/gaming, bona fide consumer transactions, creditor offsets, and lawful court orders.

headings.title: Prior offender felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Elevates repeat identity theft or attempted identity theft of credit, money, goods, services, or other property not exceeding seven hundred fifty dollars to a class E felony.

headings.title: Aggregation of offenses under single scheme
headings.reviewNote: Permits treating multiple acts attributable to a single scheme or plan as a single offense aggregating total value.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 10 subsections against archived text; tightened subsection 6 discovery standard and subsection 9 'not exceeding' threshold in notes.

headings.title: Offense of trafficking in stolen identities
headings.reviewNote: Defines trafficking in stolen identities by manufacturing, selling, or transferring means of identification for identity theft.

headings.title: Evidentiary effect of possessing five or more identities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that possession of five or more means of identification of the same person or of five or more separate persons shall be evidence of trafficking intent, excluding own or consented documents.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates trafficking in stolen identities as a class B felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text; corrected subsection 2 heading and note from 'presumption' to statutory 'shall be evidence' standard.

headings.title: Offense of misappropriation of intellectual property
headings.reviewNote: Defines misappropriation of intellectual property by unauthorized copying or commercial distribution of sound recordings and performances.

headings.title: Broadcasting and personal use exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts radio and television broadcasters, home copying for personal use, and cable television transmissions.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates misappropriation as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class D felony for repeat offenses or one hundred or more articles.

headings.title: Definitions
headings.reviewNote: Defines audiovisual works, manufacturer, motion pictures, owner, and person.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (including pre-February 15, 1972 sound recording scope in subsection 1(1)).

headings.title: Offense of facilitating theft of cable television service
headings.reviewNote: Defines facilitating cable theft by selling, manufacturing, or distributing unauthorized decoding devices, kits, or plans.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates facilitating theft of cable television service as a class D felony.

headings.title: Exemption for personal recording and satellite dishes
headings.reviewNote: Exempts ownership and operation of video cassette recorders and satellite receiving dishes for personal reception.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of operating audiovisual recording device in theater
headings.reviewNote: Defines the offense of operating an audiovisual recording device in a motion picture theater without owner consent.

headings.title: Definition of audiovisual recording function
headings.reviewNote: Defines audiovisual recording function as device capability to record or transmit motion pictures.

headings.title: Definition of motion picture theater
headings.reviewNote: Defines motion picture theater and excludes lobbies and non-viewing areas.

headings.title: Law enforcement exemption and civil immunity for theater operators
headings.reviewNote: Exempts law enforcement activities and grants conditional civil immunity to theater operators detaining suspected violators.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates theater recording as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony for prior convictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text; formerly section 578.500 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of mortgage fraud
headings.reviewNote: Defines mortgage fraud through deceptive schemes, material misstatements or omissions, receipt of fraudulent closing proceeds, or influencing appraisals through extortion or bribery (with USPAP-compliant request exceptions).

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates mortgage fraud as a class D felony.

headings.title: Separate offense for each transaction
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that each fraudulent mortgage transaction constitutes a separate punishable offense.

headings.title: Venue for prosecution
headings.reviewNote: Establishes venue rules based on property location, acts in furtherance, proceeds control, closing location, or document recording.

headings.title: Cumulative penalties
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that mortgage fraud penalties are cumulative to any other punishments provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text; aligned subsection 1 note with statutory 'extortion or bribery' appraisal wording.

headings.title: Title of act
headings.reviewNote: Cites section as the Stolen Valor Act of 2007.

headings.title: Unauthorized wear or commercial transfer of military medals
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized wearing, purchasing, selling, or manufacturing of military medals with intent to misrepresent veteran or medal status as a class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for repeat violations.

headings.title: Verbal or written misrepresentation of medal receipt
headings.reviewNote: Classifies verbal or written misrepresentation of having been awarded military decorations or medals as a class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for repeat violations.

headings.title: Fraudulent use of veteran title
headings.reviewNote: Classifies fraudulent use of the title veteran to obtain personal benefit without verifiable proof as a class A misdemeanor, or class E felony for repeat violations.

headings.title: Felony enhancement for distinguished service medals
headings.reviewNote: Elevates violations involving distinguished-service cross, silver star, purple heart, or specified medals to a class E felony.

headings.title: Felony enhancement for Medal of Honor
headings.reviewNote: Elevates violations involving the Medal of Honor to a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text (Stolen Valor Act of 2007; formerly section 578.510); noted repeat class E felony tiers in subsections 2-4 notes.

headings.title: Offense of fraud or deception in obtaining licenses or permits
headings.reviewNote: Defines fraud or deception in obtaining an instruction permit, driver license, or nondriver license, including conspiracy and assistance.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates fraud or deception in obtaining an instruction permit, driver's license, or nondriver's license as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified against archived text (formerly section 578.570); broadened subsection 1 heading to cover instruction permits, driver's licenses, and nondriver's licenses.

headings.title: Offense of mass manufacture or possession of fake IDs
headings.reviewNote: Defines mass manufacture or possession of fake IDs involving five or more fictitious or forged identities with intent to distribute.

headings.title: Penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Designates mass manufacture or possession of fake IDs as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text (effective 1-01-17).

headings.title: Offense of unlawfully receiving public assistance benefits
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawfully receiving public assistance benefits or EBT cards without lawful entitlement or approval.

headings.title: Penalty classifications and mandatory minimum imprisonment
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful receipt from class A misdemeanor to class D felony and mandates 120 days imprisonment absent timely restitution.

headings.title: Mandatory full restitution condition
headings.reviewNote: Mandates full restitution for converted funds and conditions probation release upon full payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 578.377 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of conversion of public assistance benefits
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful conversion of public assistance benefits or EBT cards to other property contrary to governing rules.

headings.title: Penalty classifications and mandatory minimum imprisonment
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful conversion from class A misdemeanor to class D felony and mandates 120 days imprisonment absent timely restitution.

headings.title: Mandatory full restitution condition
headings.reviewNote: Mandates full restitution for converted funds and conditions probation release upon full payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 578.379 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of unlawful transfer of public assistance benefits
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful transfer of public assistance benefits or EBT cards to unapproved recipients.

headings.title: Penalty classifications and mandatory minimum imprisonment
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful transfer from class A misdemeanor to class D felony and mandates 120 days imprisonment absent timely restitution.

headings.title: Mandatory full restitution condition
headings.reviewNote: Mandates full restitution for converted funds and conditions probation release upon full payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified verbatim against archived text; formerly section 578.381 (transferred 2014).

headings.title: Offense of perjury to obtain public assistance
headings.reviewNote: Defines perjury by verified written false statements to obtain assistance and prohibits dual charges with unlawful receipt.

headings.title: Materiality standard
headings.reviewNote: Defines materiality as statements that could or did substantially affect the granting of public assistance.

headings.title: Immateriality belief and incompetency defenses barred
headings.reviewNote: Specifies knowledge of materiality is not an element and precludes defenses of mistaken belief of immateriality or incompetency for reasons other than mental disability.

headings.title: Penalty classifications
headings.reviewNote: Classifies assistance perjury as a class A misdemeanor, elevated to class E or class D felony based on value or prior findings.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (formerly section 578.385); noted mental-disability carve-out in subsection 3 note.

headings.title: Investigative and subpoena authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director of social services and attorney general to issue subpoenas, examine witnesses, and inspect records.

headings.title: Judicial enforcement and contempt
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes circuit court enforcement orders and contempt proceedings for refusal to obey department or attorney general subpoenas.

headings.title: Confidentiality and disclosure exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Restricts disclosure of subpoenaed materials except for litigation, prosecutorial exchange, or internal departmental use.

headings.title: Penalty classification for improper disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Designates improper disclosure of investigative materials as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Supplemental statutory powers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that investigative authority under this section supplements rather than repeals existing legal powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text (formerly section 578.387); preserved permissive 'may' in subsections 1-2 and mandatory nondisclosure in subsection 3.
